title: Lists and Sets
subtitle: LPUSH, RPOP, SADD, SINTER, and queue patterns

content.text: Redis Lists support O(1) push and pop from both ends, making them perfect for queues and stacks.

content.code:
# Producer
RPUSH jobs "job1" "job2" "job3"

# Consumer (blocking — waits up to 30s)
BLPOP jobs 30

# Check length
LLEN jobs

content.text: Sets store unique strings. Use them for tags, followers, or any "is X in group Y?" queries.

content.code:
SADD user:1:friends "alice" "bob"
SADD user:2:friends "bob" "carol"

# Common friends
SINTER user:1:friends user:2:friends  # "bob"

questions.question: What does BLPOP do when the list is empty?
options: Blocks until an element is pushed
questions.explanation: BLPOP blocks the connection until an element is available, up to the timeout.

faq.q: How do I implement a task queue with Redis?
faq.a: RPUSH tasks to enqueue, BLPOP tasks from the other side to dequeue. Workers block on BLPOP waiting for work.
